thread:
Maya (CSM): FYI dashboard flagged ACME Retail: weekly active sessions down ~42% in last 7 days.
Jordan (CS Ops): ugh. any config or billing flags? also ping infra if there's a rollout.
Ethan (SE): their dedicated cluster had a model rollout fail on 2024-03-12; fallback served but P95 latency spiked. possible client-side throttling.
Priya (ACME PM): we shipped a UI experiment last Wed; might be related. we've also scheduled a pause on heavy syncs tomorrow.
Maya (CSM): ok. propose a two-stage playbook: rapid "stabilize" (48h) + conditional "cost-saving downgrade" path. posting checklist...
Jordan (CS Ops): share the checklist here and i'll add operational triggers and a rollback snippet.
Maya (CSM): 
```text
ACME Stabilize & Save (48h)
1) Outreach (owner: Maya) - within 4h: acknowledge, set expectation, schedule 1:1
2) Runtime triage (owner: Ethan) - 4-12h: confirm rollout state, check canary, monitor P95
3) Ops mitigations (owner: Jordan) - 12-24h: enable prefix cache, tighten batching for high-frequency endpoints
4) Short-term relief (owner: RevenueOps) - 2-week 50% burst credit on Dedicated pool
5) Enablement (owner: Maya/Liam) - 30-min session + prebuilt prompt templates
6) Feedback capture (owner: Maya) - 3-question pulse after mitigation
Escalation: If MAU drop >30% persists after 48h -> escalate to Head of CS for exec alignment with CTO
```
Ethan (SE): recommend non-invasive A/B: route 10% to a quantized variant to gauge quality vs cost before broad switches.
Liam (Support): i'll draft a concise outreach message; short, empathetic, and with clear next steps.
Priya (ACME PM): discount sounds fine but need written terms. @Zara can legal fast-track?
Jordan (CS Ops): adding rollback commands to runbook:
```bash
# rollback deployment to canary
redwood rollout revert --deployment acme-dedicated --to canary
redwood monitor latency --deployment acme-dedicated --window 10m
```
Maya (CSM): also including activation quick wins to regain perceived value:
- two prebuilt prompt templates for core endpoints
- short eval comparing canary vs current on sample prompts
- one 30-min enablement session + recording
Ethan (SE): i'll attach a lightweight eval harness and run it locally on their sample set.
Maya (CSM): timeline proposed: outreach in 1h, triage within 6h, mitigations applied within 24h, check-in at 48h. if still degraded -> propose downgrade path.
Priya (ACME PM): what does the downgrade path look like? they asked for lower-cost options without major UX regression.
Jordan (CS Ops): low-friction downgrade path:
- A: move non-critical routes to 4-bit quantized model variant
- B: enable aggressive prefix caching for bot-like flows
- C: cap max tokens on non-core completions
- D: re-evaluate after 7 days; if eval quality drop >5% rollback
Maya (CSM): suggested customer pulse post-fix: "Resolved to your satisfaction? (Y/N)", "Any features blocking you?", "Want a 30-min follow-up?"
Liam (Support): wiring the pulse into Intercom and tagging conversation with `save-plan:acme`.
Jordan (CS Ops): i'll spin up a shared doc and post link in #eng-runtime for owners and timestamps.
Jordan (CS Ops): doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/save-plans/acme-2774012345
Maya (CSM): owners assigned: Maya(outreach), Ethan(triage), Jordan(ops), Liam(support), RevenueOps(promo), Zara(legal).
Zara (Legal): can review promo terms within 6 business hours; ping if it becomes urgent.
notify-bot: Incident INC-2774012345 created: ACME MAU drop.
Maya (CSM): closing loop for now: outreach scheduled and actions in shared doc. i'll update thread as we make progress.
Ethan (SE): triage complete: reverted to canary -> P95 latency down ~45%. monitoring.
Maya (CSM): 24h update: MAU back to ~86% of baseline, promo applied, leaving open for final check.
Priya (ACME PM): running the pulse now.
Maya (CSM): survey feedback: scored 8/10, asked for more onboarding examples. adding to enablement pack.
Jordan (CS Ops): marking incident mitigated. will coordinate a runtime postmortem next week.
Maya (CSM): nice work team :tada: saved the account and captured useful feedback for follow-up.
